additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410725-DC/Si-D/SA-[Y2 / R4 312922184006] SECC/imd issue CRM:00579001564
additional_info.body:
Hello Sadek,
Greetings of the day!
We checked the logs of 5th Mar 2025 and found that-
Wed, 05 Mar 2025 01:21:51 GMT
2025-03-05, 01:21:50
2025-03-05T01:21:50.672249+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] ecog-secc-adapter/93aab349aa5b[730]:
Error polling coap://10.20.17.100:
5683/state Error: No reply in 4.25s
There was continuous Error polling coap.
Error polling coap indicates -Internal communication to SECC lost for small interval of time.
SiC D will reconnect to SECC within 5 seconds. While SECC is not reachable, an "Outlet out of order" flag will be active and will be cleared out as soon as the SiC D reconnects to SECC.
When we rebooted the charger, this error disappeared.
If the same error persists again, then you need to check the connections to KF11 and KF14 as per the diagram below:
Kindly check the KF11 itself, whether it is getting proper supply of 24V.
Hence need to check the Ecog and LAN cable.
Also at the time of error, we observed following error flags:
Flag regarding the Modbus comm to the SECC2300 (KF11) to gather the Insulation Monitor Device (Bender IMD) data
(data flow: IMD→ Modbus RTU→ SECC2300→ Modbus TCP→ PLC)
true
: modbus client (SECC) is in error/connection loss for over 750ms; it is being reset if connection established and data being sent/received
possible solution:
check the SECC2300 for proper electrical connection
check the LAN connection between SECC2300↔ PLC
restart the SECC2300 by unplugging & replugging  J1 connector (left top front)
Hope this answers your query.
Do let us know if you have any other queries or should we proceed to close this case?
Thank you
Best Regards
eMobility Tech Support Team - Vaishnavi Raut
